newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil closes $7.50 up on supply fears.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil closes $7.50 up on supply fears.

text.p: IPE November gas oil closed $7.50 a tonne higher while crude bounded to a new five-year high as a U.S. refinery fire at the weekend showed up the market's vulnerability to low heating oil stocks, brokers said.
IPE gas oil ended the day at $234.00 a tonne after coming under some light selling pressure near the close.
The market had been edgy since the open on news of renewed fighting between rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq. The United States urged Iraq and Iran to keep out of the conflict.
IPE November Brent pushed through key resistance in the afternoon to a post-Gulf War high of $24.75 a barrel.
It was trading 71 cents up at $24.69 a barrel at 1650 GMT.
"Fundamentally there has not been that much change, so a bit of Kurdish infighting and a refinery fire and that's it, off we go," a futures broker said.
Another said it just showed that things could go wrong when crude and heating oil stocks were low, which in turn made the market sensitive to any supply hiccups.
Oil and heating oil prices have held firm even though the political premium was taken out of the market when Gulf tensions eased after the first round of fighting in Iraqi Kurdistan in August.
A broker said gas oil did not appear to have kept up with the crude rally though it took its lead from stronger U.S. heating oil.

"Once the heating oil had taken off and went up to 74 (cents a gallon), then you saw some selling held," a broker said. "I don't know if we've done what we needed to do or established a range. We were reacting to news from the U.S."

With U.S. unleaded gasoline also setting a new contract high for November, the oil complex appeared to have found more balance. U.S. brokers said gasoline was still benefiting from industry data last week showing lower refinery runs and imports.
